canonical_statement: The study aimed to use retrospective clinical data to derive patient-specific initial UFH dosing that maximizes the probability of therapeutic aPTT within 4–8 hours.
The source cohort began with 4,779 unique adult MIMIC-II ICU patients who received heparin.

canonical_statement: The primary modeled outcome was aPTT 4–8 hours after the initial infusion, categorized as sub-therapeutic below 60 s, therapeutic at 60–100 s, and supra-therapeutic above 100 s.

concept.text: Therapeutic aPTT 4–8 hours after initial UFH infusion

canonical_statement: The investigators examined aPTT measurements in empirically defined windows around 6 hours (4–8 h), 12 hours (9–20 h), and 24 hours (21–32 h) after initiation.

Primary model covariates included weight-normalized heparin dose, measurement time, age, gender, white versus nonwhite ethnicity, Elixhauser score, medical versus surgical ICU type, SOFA score, creatinine, and a binary liver-injury indicator.
Liver injury was defined as AST or ALT greater than five times the upper limit of normal.
Initial heparin bolus information was unavailable for most patients and therefore was not included in the primary model.
Heparin indication could not be reliably determined for a large fraction of the cohort, so indication was omitted from the primary model and ICU type was used as a proxy.
Two independent multivariable logistic regressions modeled sub-therapeutic and supra-therapeutic aPTT using the same feature set.
The probability of therapeutic aPTT was defined as 1 minus the summed modeled probabilities of supra-therapeutic and sub-therapeutic aPTT.
Predictive validation used ten-fold cross-validation; model performance was summarized with mean AUC and Hosmer–Lemeshow calibration tests.
Three-class discrimination was evaluated with volume under the ROC surface (VUS), compared against a weight-based model, with improvement tested by likelihood-ratio test.

Alternative multinomial/ordinal logistic, neural-network, ensemble, and multiclass support-vector-machine approaches were trained/validated on 70% of data and tested on 30%; the proposed approach performed better on the held-out test portion.
At approximately 6 hours, 747 patients were sub-therapeutic, 382 therapeutic, and 382 supra-therapeutic by the study aPTT thresholds.

canonical_statement: The study modeled aPTT rather than patient-centered bleeding or thrombotic outcomes, and the authors recommended future prospective collection of anti-Xa and bleeding/thrombotic outcomes.

Some MIMIC-II observations predated or occurred during uneven rollout of the BIDMC heparin protocol, and de-identification date shifting prevented determining which patients were managed under the protocol versus physician-selected dosing.
The retrospective dataset was limited to variables recorded in routine care, leaving potentially relevant determinants such as heparin-binding proteins and complete bolus information unavailable.
The model was developed from one institution’s ICU data and had not been externally validated or prospectively tested in a randomized trial.

The authors concluded that combining logistic models can estimate a patient-specific initial dose that maximizes the probability of reaching a chosen therapeutic window and could be adapted to other medications with measurable therapeutic targets.
The authors identified external ICU validation and randomized prospective evaluation against weight-based heparin dosing as necessary next steps.
The study was supported by NIH/NIBIB grant R01 EB001659; the authors state that the sponsors had no role beyond financial support.
The authors declared no conflicts of interest and no associations perceived to affect research conduct or judgment.
